_comment: Pinned values for `dev-guardian ci-init` (Task 21). One data file so a release can refresh every SHA/checksum here in one place, instead of hunting them through three per-host YAML templates. Every action is pinned by FULL commit SHA (never a floating major-version tag like `@v7`); every scanner binary is pinned by version and a sha256 verified against the tool's own GitHub release (downloaded and independently hashed, not merely copied from the release's own checksums file). `version` fields are the human-readable comment dev-guardian appends after each pinned SHA. See README below each block for how each value was obtained and when.

actions._readme: Full commit SHA per action, verified via `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/tags` (2026-09-25; setup-node v7.1.0, codeql-action v4.39.1, upload-artifact v7.0.2 and download-artifact v8.0.2 bumped 2026-10-24, `git ls-remote` agreeing — codeql-action's annotated tag peeled to its commit; codeql-action v4.39.3 and setup-dotnet v6.1.0 bumped 2026-11-13 the same way, both immutable releases) — NOT `.../git/refs/tags/<tag>`, which resolves an ANNOTATED tag object rather than the commit it points at for some of these repos. `tags` already resolves to the commit SHA GitHub Actions itself checks out for `uses: owner/repo@<tag>`.

upload_sarif._note: github/codeql-action is a monorepo; upload-sarif is one action inside it, versioned with the whole repo's own release tags.

setup_dotnet._note: GitHub-only: scan_sast's .NET analyzers need the SDK, which gitlab/bitbucket document as a requirement instead of installing (see each template's own header comment).

setup_go._note: GitHub-only, and only on a repository with a root go.mod: gosec loads packages through the Go toolchain, the version go.mod names (`go-version-file`). Resolved 2026-10-24 with `git ls-remote --tags` (a lightweight tag: the commit itself); an immutable release, published 2026-07-16. gitlab/bitbucket document Go as a requirement instead (each template's header comment).

attest_build_provenance._note: `ci-init github --attest` only. Resolved 2026-09-28 with `gh api repos/actions/attest-build-provenance/tags` and cross-checked with `git ls-remote` (a lightweight tag: both name the same commit). Since v4 it is a composite wrapper around actions/attest, itself pinned by SHA inside it (508db95d…, v4.2.1).

upload_artifact._note: `ci-init github --attest` only: the scan job keeps the two reports for the attest job, and so anyone verifying can download what was attested. Resolved the same way, same day.

download_artifact._note: `ci-init github --attest` only: the attest job fetches the reports the scan job kept. Resolved the same way, same day.

scanners._readme: Linux amd64 binaries only — every generated pipeline template runs on a Linux CI image (ubuntu-latest / a Debian-based container). Each url/sha256 pair was downloaded and hashed independently with `sha256sum` (2026-09-25), then cross-checked against the release's own published checksums file; both agreed for all three. `archive_member` is the exact path this task found the binary at inside that same downloaded tarball (`tar -tzf`, 2026-09-25) — all three ship it bare at the archive root, not nested under a `<name>_<version>_<os>_<arch>/` directory the way some projects do; re-run `tar -tzf` against the new tarball and update this field (never assume it is unchanged) whenever a version bump changes `linux_amd64_url`. bandit/semgrep/zizmor are Python packages, not a release binary: the templates install them, with every dependency of theirs, from `configs/ci/python/<X.Y>/requirements.txt` — read from the dev-guardian clone the job verified against the release commit — into a venv of the image's own python3 (`python3 -I -m venv`, whose pip is the OS package's), with `pip install --require-hashes --only-binary :all: -r`. One lock per Python a template runs on: 3.12 (ubuntu-24.04, today's ubuntu-latest), 3.13 (node:22-trixie) and 3.14 (ubuntu-26.04, for when ubuntu-latest moves to it); a job on any other Python stops, naming the missing lock. Each lock is `uv pip compile configs/ci/python/requirements.in` (the command is its header: uv 0.13.6, `--python-platform x86_64-manylinux_2_39 --generate-hashes --only-binary :all:`), run from the repository root in python:3.12-slim on 2026-10-27; it lists every file PyPI holds for each pinned version (70 packages, 1003 sha256), and every one was matched against PyPI's JSON API, a second endpoint of the index. The install was run in ubuntu:24.04 (Python 3.12.3, pip 24.0), node:22-trixie (3.13.5, pip 25.1.1) and ubuntu:26.04 (3.14.4, pip 25.1.1): pip verified each downloaded wheel against the lock, `pip check` passed, and semgrep, bandit and zizmor each reported a finding on a sample; a lock with one hash altered was refused. Why not pipx with a hashed constraints file: pipx passes the package on the command line, and pip 24.0 and 25.1.1 refuse it under --require-hashes when its hash is only in a constraints file (pip 26.2.2 accepts it) — and pipx 1.7.1 first upgrades its own shared pip from PyPI, unpinned (`pip install --upgrade pip >= 23.1`, measured: 26.2.2), which is the very gap. Bump a version here and in requirements.in together, then recompile every lock with its header's command (test/unit/configs/pinnedCiData.test.ts fails while a lock's top-level pins differ from these versions; `npm run pins` says when a locked dependency has a newer release).

trivy._note: Same tag as TRIVY_INSTALL_TAG in mcp/src/runners/installCatalog.ts — keep both in step when either is bumped; test/unit/configs/pinnedCiData.test.ts asserts they agree.

bandit._note: bandit[toml]==<version> in configs/ci/python/requirements.in (and so in each hashed lock) — verified current on PyPI 2026-09-25; same version and [toml] extra as installCatalog.ts's own bandit entry (needed if the scanned project has a pyproject.toml `[tool.bandit]` section).

semgrep._note: semgrep==<version> in configs/ci/python/requirements.in (and so in each hashed lock) — 2026-10-24: 1.182.0 is the latest with a public tag (semgrep/semgrep v1.182.0); it requires pyjwt>=2.15.0, which fixes the advisories of the pyjwt 2.13.0 that 1.178.0 resolved to (GHSA-gvp8-978c-rx2q, GHSA-p4g4-x82p-q773, …). 2026-10-27: Trivy 0.76.1 finds two medium advisories in the lock, both in what 1.182.0 itself requires, so pipx installed them as well — mcp 1.29.0 (CVE-2026-59951, fixed in 1.30.0; semgrep requires mcp==1.29.0) and opentelemetry-api 1.37.0 (CVE-2026-114603, fixed in 1.45.1; semgrep requires ~=1.37.0). A Semgrep release that allows the fixes is the bump. 2026-11-13: 1.183.0 to 1.185.0 still require mcp==1.29.0 and opentelemetry-api>=1.37.0,<1.38 (uv's resolver, each release) — none is that bump; the repository's .trivyignore accepts the advisories that have no upgrade, each with its reason and an expiry.

zizmor._note: zizmor==<version> in configs/ci/python/requirements.in (and so in each hashed lock) — verified current on PyPI 2026-11-13 (1.32.0, published 2026-11-02); the GitHub template and the release-branch renderings still pass it with zero findings (ciInitCli.test.ts, run with 1.32.0).

gosec._note: Hashed independently and matched against gosec_2.30.0_checksums.txt, and verified with cosign verify-blob against securego/gosec's cosign.pub and the release's .sigstore.json bundle (2026-10-24); `tar -tzf` lists gosec at the archive root. Same version as PINNED_RELEASES.gosec in mcp/src/runners/installCatalog.ts — test/unit/configs/pinnedCiData.test.ts asserts they agree.

psalm._note: The release PHAR (one file for every CPU, run by php), installed only when the checkout has PHP. Hashed independently and matched against GitHub's asset digest and the psalm/phar repository's copy of the tag; psalm.phar.asc verifies with the ed25519 key bin/ci/build-phar.sh signs with (6.20.10, published 2026-11-07, checked 2026-11-13). 7.x is not taken yet: a new major, first released 2026-11-05, with a release almost every day since. Same version and sum as PSALM_VERSION / PSALM_PHAR_SHA256 in mcp/src/runners/installCatalog.ts — test/unit/configs/pinnedCiData.test.ts asserts they agree.
